validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification; keep as an active in-development India-Nepal cross-border proposal.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently corroborated bilateral proposal, not a GEM-only entity. Three separate Nepali outlets across three separate meetings confirm it by name: The Himalayan Times (2020-01-31) reports Nepal and India agreed to jointly study feasibility of a 'Gorakhpur-Rupandehi natural gas pipeline' at a Jan-2020 Nepal-India Joint Working Group (JWG) meeting; Kathmandu Post (2020-08-25) reports the 'Gorakhpur-Bhairahawa' gas pipeline (Bhairahawa is the headquarters city of Rupandehi District -- same corridor, alternate endpoint name) discussed at an Aug-2020 JWG meeting; Kathmandu Post (2023-04-30) still lists 'another proposed gas pipeline ... from Gorakhpur, India to Bhairahawa' discussed at an Apr-2023 JWG meeting. A fourth, older item (myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com, 2018-09-29, not cited -- pre-dates the sheet's own sources and adds no new independent value) shows the same corridor ('extension of natural gas pipeline from Gorakhpur of India to Sunauli-Bhairahawa of Nepal') was already on the table as far back as a Sep-2018 JWG meeting, i.e. this proposal has been discussed, unchanged, for 8 years with zero implementation progress at any point. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both correct for a proposed international trunk gas line; no re-classification needed. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 27-row India-gas in-scope roster -- no other row covers an India-Nepal corridor (P0928 India-Myanmar-Bangladesh and P0766 TAPI are different, non-overlapping cross-border corridors), so no duplicate/relabel risk. ENDPOINTS: Gorakhpur (Uttar Pradesh, India) and Rupandehi/Bhairahawa (Nepal) are named consistently across every source found, 2018-2023.

validity.recommendation: Treat LengthKnown=113 km as unverified pending a real source; consider flagging in ResearcherNotes as an unsourced estimate rather than silently carrying it as if corroborated.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's LengthKnown=113.00 km has no ref at all (MISSING_REF) and I could not find a source for it anywhere -- not in the three wiki-cited articles (none gives a distance), not via targeted web search for '113 km'/'113 kilometer' + Gorakhpur/Bhairahawa/Rupandehi (no hits), and gem.wiki's own Project Details table (read for leads only, per standing rule 1, never cited) carries the identical '70 miles / 113 kilometers' figure with NO footnote or source of its own -- i.e. this number has never been publicly sourced by GEM either, it just propagated onto the sheet. Given the project has never advanced past 'study the feasibility' (see existence note), no engineering-grade route/length has ever been published for it to source. 113 km is plausible as a rough Gorakhpur-Bhairahawa road/straight-line distance estimate but that is my inference, not a citation. Recommend leaving LengthKnown as-is (do not fabricate a ref) but note in ResearcherNotes that the figure is unconfirmed.

validity.recommendation: Owner1/Owner2 (Indian Oil Corp / Nepal Oil Corp) are plausible under the standard India-Nepal petroleum-pipeline cooperation framework but no source names them for THIS specific pipeline -- leave as-is, flag as inferred-by-framework rather than project-confirmed.
validity.researcher_notes: Every India-Nepal cross-border petroleum/gas pipeline in the bilateral JWG process (Motihari-Amlekhgunj, Amlekhgunj-Chitwan/Lothar, Siliguri-Jhapa) is implemented jointly by Indian Oil Corporation and Nepal Oil Corporation, and the 2018 myrepublica article (not cited) has the two energy ministers agreeing that 'IOC and Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC) will work together on these projects' in the same statement that lists a Gorakhpur-Sunauli-Bhairahawa gas-pipeline extension among the items discussed. That is suggestive but not a project-specific naming of IOC/NOC as owners of the Gorakhpur-Rupandehi line -- none of the three sheet-cited articles name an implementing company for this pipeline by name. Could not independently confirm Owner1=Indian Oil Corp / Owner2=Nepal Oil Corp specifically for P2213; treat as plausible-by-pattern, not verified.

fills.researcher_notes: Both endpoints are named explicitly and consistently: Himalayan Times (2020-01-31) names 'Gorakhpur in India to Rupandehi in Nepal'; Kathmandu Post (2020-08-25) names 'Gorakhpur to Bhairahawa' (Bhairahawa = headquarters city of Rupandehi District, same endpoint the sheet's EndLocation already reflects). No source gives a district/prefecture-level breakdown, so StartPrefecture/District and EndState/Province stay unsourced/blank.

No source found anywhere (sheet's own cited articles, targeted web search, or gem.wiki's own unsourced Project Details table) gives a length figure for this pipeline -- it has never progressed past a feasibility-study proposal, so no route/length has ever been published. Left UNRESOLVED rather than fabricate a ref; see the paired spec-concern validity item.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is a cross-border India-Nepal MOU-stage proposal, so PNGRB's register (which covers only the Indian domestic common-carrier grid) does not carry it and cannot be used, per the country guidance. Newest independent evidence I could find naming this specific corridor is the Kathmandu Post's 2023-04-30 report of an April-2023 Nepal-India JWG meeting, where it is STILL described as 'another proposed gas pipeline' with no progress beyond the words 'to study feasibility' first used in Jan 2020 -- three-plus years and at least four JWG meetings (2018, Jan-2020, Aug-2020, Apr-2023) produced zero forward movement on this specific line. I checked for anything more recent: the most recent Nepal-India JWG meeting I could find coverage of is the 5th meeting (scheduled Dec 8, 2025, per Asian Lite / Omm Com News / The Hindu, all dated 2025-12-03) -- its reported agenda covers ATF/aviation-fuel pipeline supply via the Lothar extension, LPG pipeline/storage, and the Siliguri-Jhapa products pipeline, with NO mention of the Gorakhpur-Rupandehi/Bhairahawa gas line. A separate March-2026 Nepal proposal for a gas pipeline (Khabarhub, 2026-03-24) is a different, unrelated corridor (Motihari-Sarlahi), not this one. So as of today (2026-08) there is no independent evidence this project has been discussed at all since April 2023 (3.3 years), and it has been implicitly dropped from the active JWG agenda in favor of other India-Nepal pipeline projects (ATF, LPG, products). Applying the dormancy rule for a 'proposed' project with no progress for >=2 years: recommend Status -> shelved, ShelvedCancelledType=inferred, no fabricated ref per standing rule 2. This is an inference from absence of evidence, not a sourced status-change announcement, so proposed_refs is intentionally empty.

summary: P2213 (Gorakhpur-Rupandehi Gas Pipeline): existence confirmed via 3 independent Nepali sources (2020-2023) naming this exact India-Nepal corridor, no duplicate/misclassification found; length (113 km) is unsourced anywhere including gem.wiki itself (UNRESOLVED); ownership (IOC/Nepal Oil Corp) is plausible-by-framework but not project-specifically confirmed; and status flagged STALE -- no evidence of any activity since an April-2023 JWG mention, dropped from the Dec-2025 JWG agenda, recommend proposed -> shelved (inferred, no fabricated ref) under the 2-year dormancy rule.
